phrases.arabic: لَمْ أَسْتَطِعِ الرَّدَّ عَلَيْكَ قَبْلَ قَلِيل
هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تُعَاوِدَ الِاتِّصَالَ بِي بَعْدَ قَلِيل؟

reply.english: Of course, I'll call you in a bit.

dialogue.speaker: Samer

dialogue.speaker: Rami

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا يَا سَامِر. جَيِّدٌ أَنَّكَ اتَّصَلْتَ.
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan yaa Saamir. jayyidun annaka ittasalta.
dialogue.english: Hello, Samer. Good that you called.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: How are you? What's new?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: لَا جَدِيد، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه. لَمْ أَسْتَطِعِ الرَّدَّ عَلَيْكَ قَبْلَ قَلِيل.
dialogue.transliteration: laa jadeed, al7amdu lillaah. lam astati3i ar-radda 3alayka qabla qaleel.
dialogue.english: Nothing new, thank God. I couldn't answer you a bit ago.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: No problem. The line was busy.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.transliteration: na3am. wa inqata3a al-ittisaalu baynanaa aydan.
dialogue.english: Yes. And the call got cut off between us too.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: اِنْتَهَى رَصِيدِي، وَنَفِدَتْ بَطَّارِيَّةُ هَاتِفِي أَيْضًا.
dialogue.transliteration: intahaa raseedee, wa nafidat battaariyyatu haatifee aydan.
dialogue.english: My credit ran out, and my phone battery died too.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: الصَّوْتُ ضَعِيف، لَا تُوجَدُ إِشَارَةٌ هُنَا.
dialogue.transliteration: as-sawtu da3eef, laa toojadu ishaaratun hunaa.
dialogue.english: The sound is weak, there's no signal here.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Of course. I'll call you in a bit.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Thanks. Goodbye.

lessons.culture: In Fusha a caller says مَعَكَ followed by their name, and answering with آلُو is normal even in formal settings. A call is kept courteous by greeting first and thanking at the end.

exercises.prompt: You answer the phone. Say hello.
exercises.tip: آلُو is how a call is picked up.

exercises.tip: مَعَكَ means 'with you': the caller names himself after it.

phrases.arabic: أَوَدُّ أَنْ نَلْتَقِيَ فِي يَوْمٍ آخَر
phrases.transliteration: awaddu an naltaqiya fee yawmin aakhar

phrases.arabic: هَلْ نَلْتَقِي بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ بَدَلًا مِنَ الصَّبَاح؟
phrases.transliteration: hal naltaqee ba3da adh-dhuhri badalan mina as-sabaa7?

phrases.arabic: سَأُقَابِلُكَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ بَدَلًا مِنْ يَوْمِ الْخَمِيس

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.english: Hello Dana, I want to change the appointment.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.english: Did something happen?

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: لَا أَسْتَطِيعُ الْحُضُورَ الْيَوْم. حَدَثَ لِي ظَرْفٌ طَارِئ.
dialogue.transliteration: laa astatee3u al-7udoora al-yawm. 7adatha lee dharfun taari2.
dialogue.english: I can't come today. Something came up for me.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.english: No problem.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: آسِف عَلَى التَّغْيِيرِ الْمُفَاجِئ. هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ نُؤَجِّلَ إِلَى الْغَد؟
dialogue.transliteration: aasif 3alaa at-taghyeeri al-mufaaji2. hal yumkinu an nu2ajjila ilaa al-ghad?
dialogue.english: Sorry for the sudden change. Can we postpone to tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.arabic: غَدًا عِنْدِي عَمَل. لِنَتَّفِقْ عَلَى يَوْمٍ يُنَاسِبُنَا مَعًا.
dialogue.english: Tomorrow I have work. Let's find a day that suits us both.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: سَأُقَابِلُكِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ بَدَلًا مِنْ يَوْمِ الْخَمِيس.
dialogue.transliteration: sa-uqaabiluki yawma al-jumu3ati badalan min yawmi al-khamees.
dialogue.english: I'll meet you Friday instead of Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.arabic: الْجُمُعَةُ مُنَاسِبَة. هَلْ نَلْتَقِي بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ بَدَلًا مِنَ الصَّبَاح؟
dialogue.transliteration: al-jumu3atu munaasiba. hal naltaqee ba3da adh-dhuhri badalan mina as-sabaa7?
dialogue.english: Friday suits me. Can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.english: Yes, in the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.transliteration: wa hal al-makaanu huwa nafsu al-makaan?
dialogue.english: And is the place still the same place?

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.english: Yes, at the same cafe.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.english: OK, agreed.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.english: Thanks for your understanding.

pair.english: Shall we meet in the afternoon?

lessons.culture: Cancelling is polite when you apologise first and give a short reason, and the other person almost always answers لَا بَأْس. In Fusha حَدَثَ لِي ظَرْفٌ طَارِئ lets you explain without giving details.

dialogue.transliteration: akhbirhu annee ittasaltu. hal ladayka raqmee?
dialogue.english: Let him know I called. Do you have my number?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، لَدَيَّ رَقْمُكِ. سَأُخْبِرُهُ فَوْرَ وُصُولِه.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, ladayya raqmuki. sa-ukhbiruhu fawra wusoolihi.
dialogue.english: Yes, I have your number. I'll tell him as soon as he arrives.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: أَبَدًا. سَأُبَلِّغُهُ الْخَبَرَ فَوْرَ عَوْدَتِه. مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
dialogue.transliteration: abadan. sa-uballighuhu al-khabara fawra 3awdatihi. ma3a as-salaama.
dialogue.english: Not at all. I'll pass him the news as soon as he's in. Goodbye.

lessons.culture: Phone manners in Fusha start with a greeting such as السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ before asking for someone. Offering to take a message and promising to pass it on the moment the person returns is standard courtesy.

dialogue.speaker: Karim

dialogue.speaker: Hadi

dialogue.english: Of course. And I'll send you a voice message.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: أَرْسِلْ لِي صُورَةً لِلْمَكَانِ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.

dialogue.english: Send me a photo of the place please.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.english: Sure. Did you read my message now?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، وَصَلَتْنِي الْآن. سَأَرُدُّ عَلَيْكَ لَاحِقًا.

lessons.culture: People in the Arab world send many voice messages instead of typing, and a chat usually opens with a greeting such as السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. Friends often type in their own dialect, while Fusha is kept for formal messages to a teacher or a workplace.

lessons.culture: Video calls keep families close when relatives live in another country, and people greet and ask about each other's health before sorting out the sound and camera. Asking هَلْ تَسْمَعُنِي؟ at the start of a call is completely normal. Fusha is the language of online classes and meetings, while family calls are usually in dialect.

challenge.title: Make a plan by phone
challenge.instructions: Write a phone conversation in Fusha in which one person calls, says who is speaking, agrees a place and a time, deals with a bad line, then changes the plan with an apology and asks the other to pass the news to a third person.
required_elements: answering the phone and saying who is speaking
a place and a time for meeting
a problem with the line or the signal
an apology and a change of plan
a message for a third person

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.english: Hello?

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: مَرْحَبًا يَا سَامِي، مَعَكَ رَنَا. أَيْنَ نَلْتَقِي غَدًا؟
dialogue.transliteration: marhaban yaa Saamee, ma3aka Ranaa. ayna naltaqee ghadan?
dialogue.english: Hello Sami, this is Rana. Where shall we meet tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.arabic: لِنَلْتَقِ فِي الْمَقْهَى. هَلِ السَّاعَةُ السَّابِعَةُ مُنَاسِبَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: linaltaqi fee al-maqhaa. hal as-saa3atu as-saabi3atu munaasiba?
dialogue.english: Let's meet at the cafe. Is 7 o'clock good?

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: اِنْقَطَعَ الِاتِّصَالُ بَيْنَنَا. هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تُعَاوِدَ الِاتِّصَالَ بِي؟
dialogue.transliteration: inqata3a al-ittisaalu baynanaa. hal yumkinuka an tu3aawida al-ittisaala bee?
dialogue.english: The call got cut off. Can you call me back?

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.arabic: طَبْعًا. آلُو رَنَا، آسِف، لَا أَسْتَطِيعُ الْحُضُورَ غَدًا.
dialogue.transliteration: tab3an. aaloo Ranaa, aasif, laa astatee3u al-7udoora ghadan.
dialogue.english: Of course. Hello Rana, sorry, I can't come tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.arabic: هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ نُؤَجِّلَ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: hal yumkinu an nu2ajjila ilaa yawmi al-jumu3a?
dialogue.english: Can we postpone to Friday?

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.english: No problem. Friday suits me.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.english: Thanks. I'll be there before you.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.english: Good. Don't be late.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: وَإِذَا اتَّصَلَ رَامِي، أَخْبِرْهُ أَنَّ الْمَوْعِدَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة.
dialogue.transliteration: wa idhaa ittasala Raamee, akhbirhu anna al-maw3ida yawma al-jumu3a.
dialogue.english: And if Rami calls, tell him the appointment is on Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.english: Certainly, I'll tell him. Goodbye.
